## 1. Learning objectives
After this lesson you can:
- write an **interface** (a list of methods that must exist) and a class that **`implements`** it;
- hold different kinds of objects in one `List<Discount>` and call the same method on all of them;
- explain **polymorphism**: the same call does different things depending on the object;
- explain when to choose an interface and when inheritance (lesson 13);
- add a new kind of discount **without editing** `Sale` or `Inventory`.

## 2. Plain-English explanation
- The shop wants discounts: 10% off this week, a PHP 50 coupon, and 20% for senior citizens and persons with
  disability (PWD). Each works differently, but a `Sale` only needs one answer: **"how much do I take off?"**
- An **interface** is a **promise**. `Discount` says: "whoever implements me can do `discountFor(subtotal)` and
  `label()`". It lists *what*, not *how*. There is no code in it.
- A class **`implements`** the interface and provides the code: `PercentDiscount`, `FixedDiscount`, `SeniorPwdDiscount`,
  `NoDiscount`. Write `@Override` on each promised method.
- **Program to the interface.** `Sale` has a field `Discount discount`. It does not say `PercentDiscount`. So it works with
  every discount, including ones written next year. We say `Sale` is **loosely coupled** to the discount classes.
- **Polymorphism** (Greek: "many shapes"): `discount.discountFor(total)` runs the code of whichever object `discount` points
  at. `Sale` has no `if (discount is a coupon) ...` chains. Adding a new discount means adding one new class.
- **Interface or parent class?** A parent class (lesson 13) says "is a kind of" and shares **data and code**
  (a `Customer` is a kind of `Person`). An interface says "can do" and shares only a **promise**. A class can extend one
  parent but implement many interfaces.
- **Composition again.** `SeniorPwdDiscount` does not copy the percent maths; it **has a** `PercentDiscount` and asks it.
- **Intentional refactor.** `Sale.total()` used to mean "the lines added up". That is now called `subtotal()`;
  `total()` means "subtotal minus discount". Lines with no discount give the same numbers as before, so every old test passes.
  `Inventory.sell` gets a second overload with a `Discount`; the 3-argument one passes `new NoDiscount()`. Loyalty points
  are earned on the **discounted** total.
- **Honest shortcuts.** `PercentDiscount` quietly clamps nonsense (150%) to 100%. Lesson 16 shows how to refuse bad input
  with an exception. The senior/PWD rule is simplified (the real one has conditions). The menu does not offer discounts yet.

## 3. Runnable sample code
`examples/PolymorphismDemo.java` — a `Greeter` interface with three classes, one list holding all three, a method that works on any, and a one-line lambda.
```
java lessons/14-interfaces-and-polymorphism/examples/PolymorphismDemo.java
```
```java
List<Greeter> greeters = List.of(new Formal(), new Casual(), new Taglish());
for (Greeter greeter : greeters) {
    System.out.println(greeter.greet("Ana"));   // each object runs ITS OWN greet
}
```

## 7. Common mistakes and troubleshooting
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `X is not abstract and does not override abstract method discountFor(int)` | The class says `implements Discount` but is missing a method | Write every method of the interface, with `public` |
| `attempting to assign weaker access privileges; was public` | Wrote `int discountFor(...)` without `public` | Methods that implement an interface must be `public` |
| `incompatible types: PercentDiscount cannot be converted to Discount` | The class forgot `implements Discount` | Add it |
| `cannot find symbol` when calling `getPercent()` on a `Discount` variable | The variable type decides what you may call | Keep a `PercentDiscount` variable, or add the method to the interface |
| A 100% discount gives a wrong, huge or negative number | `int` overflow in `subtotal * percent` | Multiply in `long`, then cast |
| Customer has 25 points instead of 20 | Points were given on the subtotal | `customer.addPurchase(sale.total())` after the discount is set |
| `new Discount()` does not compile | An interface cannot be created directly | Create one of its implementations |
